findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.message: The North Star leads with open and run. W3's control list (Retry, Diagnose, restart per context, stop-summary, preview, projects-collapse, cadence, per-engine diagnose) never inventories open or run. No Phase-3 wave delivers, traces, or gates either verb. Stop/restart/attach/Doctor get full surface treatment; open and run are assumed pre-existing and only reappear as strings in the W1 task triple and the W21 S1 script. A plan that can go GREEN through W20 without a single PRESENT/STUB/ABSENT verdict or end-to-end trace for open/run cannot claim the leading clause of the North Star is engineered—only hoped for at S1.

findings.criterion: silent zero; mislabelled empty; unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; usage either works end-to-end or fails with a named state
findings.message: W4 states that a usage rollup query returning zero rows is UNPROVEN, forces an aggregation wave, and registers the surface as pending—not 0 and not blank. That collapses three distinct research outcomes into one: (a) no aggregator/table exists, (b) aggregator exists and correctly returns empty for the window, (c) measured zero. W11 later requires a PROVEN rollup that returns zero rows today to render empty, distinct from unknown and zero_measured. Those two gates cannot both be true under the same evidence rule. As written, the rollup gate will systematically mislabel legitimate empty/zero periods as "pending aggregation," which is exactly the mislabelled-empty / silent-zero class the North Star forbids—only with a different confident wrong label.

findings.criterion: every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; no dead control
findings.message: CAPABILITY-INVENTORY is the gate that decides what surface waves may claim, yet evidence is "captured-once, replayed-many" transcripts so John is not needed live to re-run a probe. That is a convenience design that fails as science: a PRESENT verdict from a frozen transcript does not prove the control is still wired when W10–W19 ship; a STUB transcript from seed output can be fixed in code while the inventory still says STUB (or the reverse). There is no re-probe obligation, staleness bound, or hash-link from inventory row to the code under test at surface-wave time. Surface waves can therefore render "working" against an obsolete capability claim—or skip a real build because an old PRESENT was replayed. For dead-control and E2E honesty, inventory-as-snapshot is not inventory-as-evidence.

findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every surface fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Wave 6 NamedState; Hardening-gate obligations (failure-state table vocabulary); wave-local failure-states/*
findings.message: The plan simultaneously asserts (1) NamedState enum {ok, unknown, empty, zero_measured, pending, unmeasured, measurement_failed, timeout, cannot_retry} as the single render primitive, and (2) the journal-0080 five-row vocabulary {dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid} with status code + user-visible text per surface verb. Wave-local tables only promise "unknown and empty as separate rows." There is no mapping table, no requirement that each of the five 0080 rows appear in each surface file, and no test that a dependency-returns-garbage path cannot render as empty or zero. The hardening section says a claim without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER; here both schemas are claimed and neither is forced into the other. Conformance can pass tri-state fixtures while the five required honesty rows are never exercised—leaving the confident-wrong-answer class unenforced.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.section: Waves 10–19 done-when / Intent; Wave 21; North Star S1 clause
findings.message: Wave intents repeatedly say "Close criterion N" (attach, usage, cost, Doctor, stop/restart, preview, projects, cadence) on the basis of scoped pytest, fault injectors, and generated HTML. W21 correctly blocks the unqualified North Star string until S1, but the plan still treats structural GREEN as criterion closure for ten criteria before any live open/run/stop/restart/Doctor/attach session with John. That is a silent claim of build success by another name: the status string is careful; the wave contract language is not. A skeptical researcher reads "close criterion 4" after W13 as a knowledge claim the evidence design forbids until S1. Either waves must say "structurally candidate only; criterion remains open until S1" with freeze/traceability reflecting that, or S1 must be an intermediate gate before any "closed" stamp—not only a terminal ceremony.

findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose and session attach; open, run, stop, and restart
findings.message: The hard-blocking evidence floor is a three-task triple: open / run / stop-restart. Doctor diagnose and session attach—named in the North Star in the same breath—are not in the triple, not John-confirmed at Phase 0, and only appear in the S1 script at the end. Phase 1 inventory may list Diagnose and Retry, but the reproducible verification tasks John signs do not. The research design therefore front-loads evidence for a subset of the North Star and postpones the attach/Doctor half until after all surface waves claim readiness. That is selection bias in the verification sample: the tasks that are easiest to schedule as "confirmation lines" are not the full phenomenon under test.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: The plan hinges dollar honesty on a cost spot-check that, if wrong, forces measurement_failed and blocks E2. It never specifies the population (which engines, which window), the independent source-row sum procedure, the agreement tolerance, who may not compute both sides, or what sample size constitutes a check versus an anecdote. Without a replicable protocol, "disagrees with the source rows" is an unfalsifiable gate: any convenient pair of numbers can pass or fail. Cost fabrication can then survive as an under-specified check that tests assert exists, not that dollars are true.

findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose; surfaces that claim diagnose work end-to-end or fail named
findings.message: "Real diagnosis" is proven by: two induced faults produce different rendered findings, non-canned output, and banner payload presence. That refutes only the weakest straw man (identical hard-coded string). It does not refute a multi-branch stub that maps fault-inject tags to polished text, nor prove findings correspond to independent ground truth outside the injector. Banner payload "not re-derived from scratch" is asserted without defining what re-derivation looks like in the artifact. For a skeptical researcher, variation under a co-located fault harness is not end-to-end diagnose honesty on real Anchor work—the North Star's Doctor clause.

findings.criterion: 3 rollups remain UNPROVEN, and W11 accepts permanent labelled pending as success for those tiles. Named pending is better than silent zero, but the North Star also requires that surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail named—not that they may forever claim usage while only showing pending. Without a freeze-time rule (aggregate-or-remove-claim) or a hard cap on pending-as-GO, the plan can "meet" criterion 3 by never measuring usage at all.
findings.message: UNPROVEN rollups "require" an aggregation wave and freeze/amendment procedure, but no wave is pre-allocated, no freeze rule forbids stamping while

findings.criterion: no preview that dumps raw binary; file preview human-friendly
findings.message: W17's entire strategy is "reuse the already-working new-window renderer" for docx/pptx/xlsx/pdf. W3 inventories a "preview path" but the plan never requires a PRESENT transcript of that shared path before W17, nor a STUB→build-it branch if the path is theater. "Already-working" is an untested premise. If the shared path is missing, partial, or itself dumps binary for one format, the wave's fixtures can still pass against a mock while production preview remains the raw-binary failure mode the North Star names.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Success criteria; Wave 13 banner_handoff; Wave 19 cadence
findings.message: Health is named alongside usage and diagnose in the North Star. The plan covers diagnose deeply and cadence/status as "status," but the health banner is only a payload handoff into Doctor—not a surface wave with PROVEN data, tri-state fixtures, or failure-state table for the banner's own health claim. A banner that shows confident green/red from unproven or empty inputs is a health surface lying while Doctor is honest. There is no wave that inventories, gates, or traces "claims health" the way W11/W12 gate usage/cost.

findings.criterion: Projects collapsed by default; preference remembered (success criteria supporting open/run UX without mislabelled empty); honesty of stored state
findings.message: W18 claims per-user collapse preference that survives reload across two profiles, with a named unknown state when the store is unreadable. The hardening section requires atomic temp+fsync+rename, cross-process lock or documented serialization, and concurrency tests when durability is claimed. W18 deliverables name none of these, and no repeat-invocation or two-process test appears in its GWT. Dual-profile tests can pass on a racy or partially written store that later surfaces as wrong expanded/collapsed state—mislabelled empty/unknown relative to what the user actually chose—without tripping any stated gate.

findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; no dead control / silent zero (honesty property); containment of v1.1.x shipping risk where escape paths matter
findings.message: The plan marks honesty, idempotence, boundedness, and containment as "asserted by this plan," and states that a named property without a checklist entry—or a claim without a matching obligation—is a BLOCKER. Surface waves do emphasize failure-state files and unknown≠empty. They do not name numeric bounds or refusal paths for inventory reads, rollup row sets, preview bytes, or trace artifacts; almost none state a repeat-invocation idempotence test; containment escape tests are centered on planning/ write smoke, not on preview/path/preference handlers that read user-controlled paths. The checklist is emitted; the wave contracts do not bind it. That is a paper guarantee of the honesty/containment properties the North Star depends on.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Continuous surface work (W10–W19) has no mandatory dead_control_audit; only W20 sweeps. Individual waves hide Retry/Diagnose when unavailable, but dual competing restart controls, leftover dead buttons on non-focal surfaces, and regressions introduced while fixing another criterion are only global-audited after all criteria claim closure. That is late detection for the primary North Star defect class. Not a missing feature—timing of the only global proof.

findings.criterion: silent zero; every usage surface works end-to-end or fails with a named state; (cost half correctly bans E2 for dollars)
findings.message: W2 correctly forbids E2 for dollars. W11 still allows a signed E2 that ships a usage/time numeral with as_of and a reconciliation log entry. A skeptical researcher treats a provisional number next to a small stamp as still a confident quantitative claim—closer to fabricated certainty than to pending/unmeasured—unless the named state machine forbids bare numerals under E2 and forces a provisional-labelled state as the primary visible text. as_of alone does not discharge the silent-wrong-number risk for usage.

Document header says `node scripts/run-all-tests.mjs` while every wave gate is scoped pytest. Inconsistent operator entrypoint; does not by itself create a dead control or fabricated dollar. Demoted under inclusion test.

findings.criterion: 1’s narrower “Retry, Diagnose, restart” success-criteria wording. That wording itself under-specifies the North Star’s leading verbs and must be expanded or the missing waves added.
findings.message: The North Star leads with four verbs — open, run, stop, restart. The plan’s Phase-3 surface train covers attach, usage/time, cost, Doctor, stop-summary, restart, preview, projects-collapse, and cadence. There is no surface wave that owns **open** or **run** as first-class controls (dead-control contract, named cannot-*, failure-state table, e2e trace). W1 only records a task triple that *includes* open/run as human confirmation items; nothing later forces those controls to work or be hidden. A competitor that ships the full work loop would treat open and run as load-bearing product surfaces, not ambient preconditions. As written, the build can go GREEN on stop/restart/attach while open/run remain dead or silent — and still claim the North Star via S1 partial pass or

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Waves 8–19 gate-commands; W9 trace schema; Success criteria “works end-to-end”
findings.message: Every surface wave’s “e2e” is `generate_html` / visible-text-node assertions plus `node --check` on script blocks, with a JSON “control→handler→capability→state” trace. That is unit-level render theater, not a user path. A competitor product proves end-to-end by driving the real UI (click Diagnose, attach from the session list, open a .docx, stop a live session) against a real or high-fidelity Anchor process and asserting the live DOM/state. This plan can pass every scoped pytest while the real control remains unbound in the served app, the click never reaches the handler, or the preview path only works in the fixture harness. “Works end-to-end” in the North Star is a user claim; HTML-string GREEN is a competitor’s favorite false green. Require at least one real interaction path per North-Star surface (or an honest named degradation if the host cannot automate UI), not only rendered-string conformance.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control … Doctor diagnose and session attach … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: W3 freezes PRESENT/STUB/ABSENT from “captured-once, replayed-many” transcripts so John is not needed live. A competitor inventory re-probes the live v1.2 surface (or fails closed to unknown) at freeze and again before each surface wave GO. One-shot replay lets a control go PRESENT on an old transcript while the real handler is now a no-op, canned, or unbound — then W13–W16 “wire it / build it” decisions and dead-control audits inherit a lie. That is exactly how dead Diagnose/Retry/restart survive a “capability-backed” plan. Capture-once is fine for offline unit tests; it is illegal as the sole authority for PRESENT that authorizes shipping a live control. Either re-probe at freeze + pre-surface GO, or treat aged transcripts as unknown and force re-inventory — never PRESENT-by-replay alone.

findings.criterion: silent zero … unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero … Cost never fabricates dollars (and usage surfaces that claim numbers must not fabricate confidence)
findings.section: Wave 11 (E2 as_of provisional usage/time); Wave 2 E2 rules; Success criteria usage/time/cost
findings.message: Cost correctly bans E2 and fabricated dollars. Usage/time still allow a signed E2 “provisional” count with an as_of stamp. A competitor usage surface never shows a numeral until the rollup is PROVEN; provisional is still a confident wrong answer — the defect class the honesty gate names. An as_of stamp next to a wrong count is a disclaimer, not honesty. If the rollup is UNPROVEN, the only competitive-grade states are pending/unknown/measurement_failed — not a number under E2. Close E2 for any user-visible count that criterion 3 surfaces (usage and time), or the plan institutionalizes silent-wrong (cousin of silent zero) on half of the usage/time/cost criterion while being strict only on dollars.

findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose … real diagnose (success criteria: Doctor real diagnose; banner payload)
findings.section: Wave 13 done-when / GWT; criterion 4 Doctor real diagnose
findings.message: W13’s proof that diagnosis is “real” is: two induced faults produce *different* rendered findings. A competitor Doctor is real when findings track injected root causes with structured, checkable claims (and non-canned content), not when two templates differ. Seeded multi-branch theater still “differs” and still fails the North Star’s “real diagnose.” Require fault→expected finding contracts (or inventory-backed golden transcripts of real diagnose behavior), plus an explicit ban on fixed seed strings — variance alone is a competitor-beatable bar.

findings.criterion: 4/health to every health-claiming surface, or the plan closes “diagnose” while leaving health claims free to silent-zero and mislabelled-empty.
findings.section: Success criteria; Wave 13 banner_handoff; North Star “health, usage, or diagnose”
findings.message: Usage and diagnose get full surface trains; “health” is reduced to banner→Doctor payload handoff. There is no wave that inventories every surface that *claims* health (banner copy, health tile, status chrome) and forces ok/unknown/empty/zero_measured/failed with unknown≠empty. A competitor health strip that shows green/empty/zero without evidence loses users to an honest unknown. Expand

findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor + attach without dead controls; surfaces work E2E or named failure
findings.section: Wave 3 STUB→build it; Wave 5 DOC-TRIO-AMENDMENT / WAVE-LIST-FREEZE
findings.message: The competitive product scopes “build it vs wire it” before committing the surface train. This plan discovers STUBs in W3, then relies on mid-build wave insertion and re-freeze. That is honest process, but it leaves the delivered North Star set unbounded: enough STUBs and the conjunction scorer (2-per-criterion / 4 total) or schedule pressure pushes E1/E3 exits or dropped surfaces. Competitor plans either (a) pre-budget a fixed maximum of build-it waves with explicit cut-line to named unavailable states, or (b) inventory before freeze with a hard cap on unsigned STUBs. Without a hard scope/cut-line tied to the ten criteria, “freeze then amend forever” is how dead controls become signed exits or unshipped work while process stays GREEN.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart … Doctor diagnose and session attach; Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.section: Wave 1 task triple; Wave 21 S1; Steward/S1 North Star clause
findings.message: S1-as-sole North Star declaration is correct and must stay. Competitor *engineering* still re-runs the verification task triple (or an automated subset) after each surface wave that claims a verb in that triple — attach after W10, diagnose after W13/W14, stop/restart after W15/W16 — so failures are cheap and early. This plan explicitly avoids live John until S1 and relies on fixture/fault injection in between. That maximizes late BUILD_BLOCKING discovery after twenty waves of process and partial product. Keep S1 as the only *declaration* of North Star met; add mandatory mid-build task-triple checkpoints (or host-automated equivalents) so “not a silent claim” is not paired with “first real user proof is also the last.”

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart … without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty, or a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: A competitor team ships the smallest honest product first: named-state primitive + the dead controls John hits daily (Diagnose, Retry/attach, restart, binary preview). This plan serializes nine Phase-0/1/2 waves (task triple, exit register, inventory, rollup gate, freeze, named state, cost_state, conformance harness, trace/fault/log) before any Phase-3 surface can start, then serializes surfaces through W19. The machinery serves honesty, but the critical path maximizes calendar risk that S1 fails or exits accumulate. Competitor sequencing: W6-class named state + one or two highest-pain surfaces in parallel with inventory/rollup, freeze only what those surfaces need. As written, the plan optimizes for process completeness over competitive time-to-honest-UX on the North Star’s daily path.

findings.criterion: a preview that dumps raw binary … File preview human-friendly Office/PDF via shared path
findings.section: Wave 17 File preview; Wave 3 inventory “preview path”
findings.message: W17 “reuses the already-working new-window renderer.” That is a competitor foot-gun: if the shared path is STUB, format-incomplete, or only works for one type, the wave becomes a thin router over a broken dependency and binary can still appear on alternate code paths. Inventory must prove PRESENT per format (docx/pptx/xlsx/pdf) with transcripts of human-friendly output *before* W17 is allowed to claim reuse; if STUB, W17 is a build-it wave for the renderer itself, not a wire-up. Competitor products do not ship “delegate to shared path” without per-format evidence the path actually humanizes those bytes.

findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.section: Wave 21 release_guard.py; North Star v1.1.x clause; Wave 1 containment
findings.message: Containment smoke protects planning-path writes and root foreign Foreman artifacts; the only explicit “not publishable to v1.1.x” guard is W21. A competitor release process fails closed on branch/channel from the first product commit (W6+). Late-only release_guard allows accidental packaging, tag, or channel bleed during surface waves. Move branch/channel non-publish checks to an early always-on gate (or extend W1 containment to publish surfaces), not only the terminal wave.

findings.criterion: exactly one restart control per restart context — work or not shown; no dual competing controls
findings.message: The audit asserts control count == 1 in rendered HTML. A competitor also proves behavioral exclusivity: only one control can trigger restart for that context (no hidden keyboard path, menu duplicate, or second entry point that restarts with a different preserved/lost contract). Count-of-buttons GREEN with two behavioral restart paths still violates “exactly one restart control per context.” Extend the contract to “exactly one restart *action* per context,” not only one labelled button in the HTML snapshot.

findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; named, user-visible state
findings.section: Hardening-gate obligations Failure-state table vocabulary; Waves 10–19 failure-states/*
findings.message: The emitted 0080 vocabulary (dependency-missing, index read/write, rebuild, reconcile, verify, CLI verbs) reads like a storage/index product, not Anchor session/Doctor/cost UI. Wave-local tables partially re-map, but the plan still requires those five rows “per surface (index read/write…).” A competitor names the states the *user* hits (attach timeout, unmeasured cost, inventory unreadable, unsupported preview). If agents fill index-reconcile rows for a Doctor tile, honesty theater returns. Require surface-native failure rows that map 1:1 to NamedState/user-visible strings for each North-Star surface; keep storage vocabulary only where the surface actually is a store/CLI.

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.section: Success criteria; Waves 10–19; Wave 1 task triple
findings.message: The North Star leads with four verbs. The plan names a verification task triple of open/run/stop-restart in W1, then spends surface waves on attach, usage, cost, Doctor, stop summary, restart, preview, projects, and cadence. There is no wave whose done-when is “open real Anchor work works end-to-end or fails with a named state,” and none for “run.” Stop and restart get W15–W16; attach gets W10. Open and run are either assumed already perfect (unproven in this draft) or silently omitted. A bored investor funds open/run/stop/restart; this plan only budgets the last half and a side attach. Either add open/run surface waves bound to inventory PRESENT|STUB|ABSENT, or freeze an explicit inventory verdict that open/run are PRESENT with transcripts and no further work—do not leave the first two North Star verbs as ambient hope.

findings.criterion: without meeting … a silent zero, a mislabelled empty … (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: W11’s acceptance says a PROVEN rollup that “genuinely returns zero rows for today” renders empty, “distinct from both unknown and zero_measured.” Zero rows for a measured day is measured zero activity, not an empty collection in the “no data domain” sense. Teaching the surface to label measured absence of events as empty reintroduces the exact mislabelled-empty / silent-zero class the North Star bans—especially once cost and usage sit on the same chrome. Empty must mean “no series / no scope,” zero_measured must mean “rollup ran and the total is 0,” unknown must mean “we did not successfully read.” Fix the Given/When/Then and the failure-state table before this wave can claim criterion 3.

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.section: Wave 5 — Wave-list freeze + doc-trio amendment; Wave 3 inventory
findings.message: W3 can reclassify any control to STUB → “build it,” and W5’s DOC-TRIO-AMENDMENT lets those waves be inserted indefinitely with only a re-freeze. There is no cap on inserted waves, no “must still hit S1 on this effort,” and no rule that STUB on a North Star control is either built in-plan or closed with a signed exit—not deferred forever by amendment churn. Bored-investor read: inventory is a blank check that can keep surface delivery (Diagnose, attach, restart) off the calendar forever while still looking “governed.” Bound it: max inserted waves, or mandatory E1/build-now decision per North Star control at freeze, with conjunction scorer already treating serial deferral as re-baseline risk.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: The plan’s own law says a property named without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER—and conversely that obligations must be enforced. Honesty (failure-state table; unknown≠empty) is partially wave-local. Idempotence (repeat-invocation), boundedness (numeric bound + refusal), containment (escape-attempt), and storage vocabulary (atomic temp+fsync+rename, cross-process lock, concurrency test) appear as global checklists with no wave that names the bound, the refusal path, the escape test, or the durable write path for preference store (W18), cost migration (W7), inventory/rollup artifacts, or EXECUTION-LOG. Claiming durability/honesty guarantees while product surfaces only assert “three labels differ” is confident process theater: the North Star needs failure honesty on real health/usage/diagnose paths, not a second copy of journal 0080 with unchecked boxes. Either map each obligation to a concrete wave acceptance criterion or drop the claim so the plan does not advertise unenforced guarantees.

findings.criterion: fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.section: Wave 6 NamedState; Hardening failure-state table vocabulary; wave-local failure-states/*
findings.message: W6 ships NamedState (ok, unknown, empty, zero_measured, pending, unmeasured, measurement_failed, timeout, cannot_retry). Hardening vocabulary demands five different rows (dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid) with status codes per surface verb. Surface waves only promise “unknown and empty as separate rows.” No mapping table says which NamedState is dependency-returns-garbage vs backing-store-unreadable. Two parallel honesty languages means implementers will satisfy the easier checklist and leave the required five as prose. That is how “named state” becomes “we showed unknown somewhere.” Require one vocabulary (or an explicit bijection enforced by the table validator) before any surface wave is GO.

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: Nine waves of ledgers, exit registers, inventory, rollup gates, freeze stamps, named-state primitives, cost enums, conformance harnesses, and trace plumbing precede the first user-facing attach honesty (W10). None of W1–W9 lets John open, run, stop, restart, diagnose, or attach on v1.2. Bored investor: all capital can be spent and still deliver zero North Star verbs if Phase 0/1/2 stalls. Process floor is defensible; a fully serial nine-wave tax before any vertical slice is not. Collapse or parallelize Phase 2 primitives with one thin end-to-end path (e.g. attach or Diagnose) so a mid-build halt still leaves a working surface, not only green pytest on governance modules.

findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose and session attach … Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose
findings.message: Attach (W10) blocks usage (W11) blocks cost (W12) blocks Doctor (W13–14) blocks stop (W15) blocks restart (W16) blocks preview (W17) blocks projects (W18) blocks cadence (W19). Doctor does not need usage tiles; restart does not need PDF preview; cadence does not need projects collapse. Artificial total order delays diagnose and restart—the named North Star inclusions—behind unrelated surfaces. Investor view: longest possible critical path maximizes calendar risk of never reaching S1 with the verbs that matter. Re-express dependencies as true data/contract edges (named_state, rollup_registry, inventory row) only; allow parallel surface waves after freeze.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build. / John can open, run, stop, and restart…
findings.section: Wave 1 task triple; Wave 5 freeze; Wave 21 S1
findings.message: W1 forbids E5 on the task triple and HALTs without John’s dated line; W5 requires John’s Phase-1 verdict review before any surface wave; W21 requires live S1. S1 as the only North Star claim is correct and in-scope. Stacking two additional hard live-John gates before any product wave means the build cannot advance through process phases without calendar attendance—while the North Star still depends on a fourth live session at the end. Bored investor: three human appointments on the critical path, two of them before value. Keep S1 sacred; make W1/W5 either pre-seedable from a prior signed artifact with expiry, or allow orchestration to proceed on captured transcripts with a single re-confirm at freeze—not a hard stop that strandsthe entire NS delivery on scheduling.

findings.criterion: without meeting … a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: W17 intent and deliverables assume “the already-working new-window path” and only “route” formats through it. That assumption is not bound to a W3 PRESENT verdict or a freeze delta. If inventory says STUB/ABSENT, this wave as written ships theater or a dead path—exactly the raw-binary / dead-control failure mode. Freeze must either insert a build-it wave for the shared renderer or mark ABSENT with a named unsupported state for all Office/PDF; W17 must not hard-code “already-working.”

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: There is no milestone where a single North Star verb is done under real UI with named failure states before the full ten-criteria matrix. Governance is front-loaded; product is back-loaded. If conjunction re-baseline HALTs at four exits mid-surface phase, John may have exit_register.py and freeze stamps but still meet dead Diagnose or dishonest attach. Define an ordered minimum slice (e.g. attach + stop + one restart context + Diagnose) that may reach a partial honest state without claiming full North Star—explicitly partial, not silent green—so investment is not all-or-nothing at W21.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: W7 adds a schema migration and backfill to unmeasured, and bans $0.00 fabrication at render time. It does not specify failed-migration behavior, partial backfill, or what the UI shows if cost_state column is missing mid-deploy—i.e. dependency-missing / backing-store paths from the plan’s own failure vocabulary. A half-migrated DB is the classic path back to “0 ⇒ subscription” or blank dollars. Require named measurement_failed/unmeasured when schema or backfill is incomplete, and a gate that refuses measured rendering until migration attestation is host-verified.

reviews.note: Skeptical-researcher angle. Fresh context only; findings judged against the North Star. Process-only nits that do not threaten a North-Star criterion are omitted or demoted.

findings.topic: open/run missing from inventory and waves
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.message: The North Star leads with open and run. W3's control list (Retry, Diagnose, restart per context, stop-summary, preview, projects-collapse, cadence, per-engine diagnose) never inventories open or run. No Phase-3 wave delivers, traces, or gates either verb. Stop/restart/attach/Doctor get full surface treatment; open and run are assumed pre-existing and only reappear as strings in the W1 task triple and the W21 S1 script. A plan that can go GREEN through W20 without a single PRESENT/STUB/ABSENT verdict or end-to-end trace for open/run cannot claim the leading clause of the North Star is engineered—only hoped for at S1.

findings.criterion: silent zero; mislabelled empty; unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; usage either works end-to-end or fails with a named state
findings.message: W4 states that a usage rollup query returning zero rows is UNPROVEN, forces an aggregation wave, and registers the surface as pending—not 0 and not blank. That collapses three distinct research outcomes into one: (a) no aggregator/table exists, (b) aggregator exists and correctly returns empty for the window, (c) measured zero. W11 later requires a PROVEN rollup that returns zero rows today to render empty, distinct from unknown and zero_measured. Those two gates cannot both be true under the same evidence rule. As written, the rollup gate will systematically mislabel legitimate empty/zero periods as "pending aggregation," which is exactly the mislabelled-empty / silent-zero class the North Star forbids—only with a different confident wrong label.

findings.topic: captured-once transcript as live capability proof
findings.criterion: every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; no dead control
findings.message: CAPABILITY-INVENTORY is the gate that decides what surface waves may claim, yet evidence is "captured-once, replayed-many" transcripts so John is not needed live to re-run a probe. That is a convenience design that fails as science: a PRESENT verdict from a frozen transcript does not prove the control is still wired when W10–W19 ship; a STUB transcript from seed output can be fixed in code while the inventory still says STUB (or the reverse). There is no re-probe obligation, staleness bound, or hash-link from inventory row to the code under test at surface-wave time. Surface waves can therefore render "working" against an obsolete capability claim—or skip a real build because an old PRESENT was replayed. For dead-control and E2E honesty, inventory-as-snapshot is not inventory-as-evidence.

findings.section: Wave 6 NamedState; Hardening-gate obligations (failure-state table vocabulary); wave-local failure-states/*
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every surface fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: The plan simultaneously asserts (1) NamedState enum {ok, unknown, empty, zero_measured, pending, unmeasured, measurement_failed, timeout, cannot_retry} as the single render primitive, and (2) the journal-0080 five-row vocabulary {dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid} with status code + user-visible text per surface verb. Wave-local tables only promise "unknown and empty as separate rows." There is no mapping table, no requirement that each of the five 0080 rows appear in each surface file, and no test that a dependency-returns-garbage path cannot render as empty or zero. The hardening section says a claim without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER; here both schemas are claimed and neither is forced into the other. Conformance can pass tri-state fixtures while the five required honesty rows are never exercised—leaving the confident-wrong-answer class unenforced.

findings.section: Waves 10–19 done-when / Intent; Wave 21; North Star S1 clause
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: Wave intents repeatedly say "Close criterion N" (attach, usage, cost, Doctor, stop/restart, preview, projects, cadence) on the basis of scoped pytest, fault injectors, and generated HTML. W21 correctly blocks the unqualified North Star string until S1, but the plan still treats structural GREEN as criterion closure for ten criteria before any live open/run/stop/restart/Doctor/attach session with John. That is a silent claim of build success by another name: the status string is careful; the wave contract language is not. A skeptical researcher reads "close criterion 4" after W13 as a knowledge claim the evidence design forbids until S1. Either waves must say "structurally candidate only; criterion remains open until S1" with freeze/traceability reflecting that, or S1 must be an intermediate gate before any "closed" stamp—not only a terminal ceremony.

findings.topic: task triple omits Doctor and attach
findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose and session attach; open, run, stop, and restart
findings.message: The hard-blocking evidence floor is a three-task triple: open / run / stop-restart. Doctor diagnose and session attach—named in the North Star in the same breath—are not in the triple, not John-confirmed at Phase 0, and only appear in the S1 script at the end. Phase 1 inventory may list Diagnose and Retry, but the reproducible verification tasks John signs do not. The research design therefore front-loads evidence for a subset of the North Star and postpones the attach/Doctor half until after all surface waves claim readiness. That is selection bias in the verification sample: the tasks that are easiest to schedule as "confirmation lines" are not the full phenomenon under test.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: The plan hinges dollar honesty on a cost spot-check that, if wrong, forces measurement_failed and blocks E2. It never specifies the population (which engines, which window), the independent source-row sum procedure, the agreement tolerance, who may not compute both sides, or what sample size constitutes a check versus an anecdote. Without a replicable protocol, "disagrees with the source rows" is an unfalsifiable gate: any convenient pair of numbers can pass or fail. Cost fabrication can then survive as an under-specified check that tests assert exists, not that dollars are true.

findings.topic: diagnose reality tested only by output variation
findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose; surfaces that claim diagnose work end-to-end or fail named
findings.message: "Real diagnosis" is proven by: two induced faults produce different rendered findings, non-canned output, and banner payload presence. That refutes only the weakest straw man (identical hard-coded string). It does not refute a multi-branch stub that maps fault-inject tags to polished text, nor prove findings correspond to independent ground truth outside the injector. Banner payload "not re-derived from scratch" is asserted without defining what re-derivation looks like in the artifact. For a skeptical researcher, variation under a co-located fault harness is not end-to-end diagnose honesty on real Anchor work—the North Star's Doctor clause.

findings.topic: unproven rollup has no forced aggregation wave
findings.criterion: 3 rollups remain UNPROVEN, and W11 accepts permanent labelled pending as success for those tiles. Named pending is better than silent zero, but the North Star also requires that surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail named—not that they may forever claim usage while only showing pending. Without a freeze-time rule (aggregate-or-remove-claim) or a hard cap on pending-as-GO, the plan can "meet" criterion 3 by never measuring usage at all.

If the shared path is missing, partial, or itself dumps binary for one format, the wave's fixtures can still pass against a mock while production preview remains the raw-binary failure mode the North Star names.

findings.section: Success criteria; Wave 13 banner_handoff; Wave 19 cadence
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Health is named alongside usage and diagnose in the North Star. The plan covers diagnose deeply and cadence/status as "status," but the health banner is only a payload handoff into Doctor—not a surface wave with PROVEN data, tri-state fixtures, or failure-state table for the banner's own health claim. A banner that shows confident green/red from unproven or empty inputs is a health surface lying while Doctor is honest. There is no wave that inventories, gates, or traces "claims health" the way W11/W12 gate usage/cost.

findings.criterion: Projects collapsed by default; preference remembered (success criteria supporting open/run UX without mislabelled empty); honesty of stored state
findings.message: W18 claims per-user collapse preference that survives reload across two profiles, with a named unknown state when the store is unreadable. The hardening section requires atomic temp+fsync+rename, cross-process lock or documented serialization, and concurrency tests when durability is claimed. W18 deliverables name none of these, and no repeat-invocation or two-process test appears in its GWT. Dual-profile tests can pass on a racy or partially written store that later surfaces as wrong expanded/collapsed state—mislabelled empty/unknown relative to what the user actually chose—without tripping any stated gate.

findings.topic: property gates asserted without wave enforcement
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; no dead control / silent zero (honesty property); containment of v1.1.x shipping risk where escape paths matter
findings.message: The plan marks honesty, idempotence, boundedness, and containment as "asserted by this plan," and states that a named property without a checklist entry—or a claim without a matching obligation—is a BLOCKER. Surface waves do emphasize failure-state files and unknown≠empty. They do not name numeric bounds or refusal paths for inventory reads, rollup row sets, preview bytes, or trace artifacts; almost none state a repeat-invocation idempotence test; containment escape tests are centered on planning/ write smoke, not on preview/path/preference handlers that read user-controlled paths. The checklist is emitted; the wave contracts do not bind it. That is a paper guarantee of the honesty/containment properties the North Star depends on.

findings.topic: dead-control audit only at final sweep
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Continuous surface work (W10–W19) has no mandatory dead_control_audit; only W20 sweeps. Individual waves hide Retry/Diagnose when unavailable, but dual competing restart controls, leftover dead buttons on non-focal surfaces, and regressions introduced while fixing another criterion are only global-audited after all criteria claim closure. That is late detection for the primary North Star defect class. Not a missing feature—timing of the only global proof.

findings.topic: E2 provisional counts still render numerals
findings.criterion: silent zero; every usage surface works end-to-end or fails with a named state; (cost half correctly bans E2 for dollars)
findings.message: W2 correctly forbids E2 for dollars. W11 still allows a signed E2 that ships a usage/time numeral with as_of and a reconciliation log entry. A skeptical researcher treats a provisional number next to a small stamp as still a confident quantitative claim—closer to fabricated certainty than to pending/unmeasured—unless the named state machine forbids bare numerals under E2 and forces a provisional-labelled state as the primary visible text. as_of alone does not discharge the silent-wrong-number risk for usage.

findings.criterion: 1’s narrower “Retry, Diagnose, restart” success-criteria wording. That wording itself under-specifies the North Star’s leading verbs and must be expanded or the missing waves added.
findings.message: The North Star leads with four verbs — open, run, stop, restart. There is no surface wave that owns **open** or **run** as first-class controls (dead-control contract, named cannot-*, failure-state table, e2e trace). W1 only records a task triple that *includes* open/run as human confirmation items; nothing later forces those controls to work or be hidden. A competitor that ships the full work loop would treat open and run as load-bearing product surfaces, not ambient preconditions. As written, the build can go GREEN on stop/restart/attach while open/run remain dead or silent — and still claim the North Star via S1 partial pass or

findings.section: Waves 8–19 gate-commands; W9 trace schema; Success criteria “works end-to-end”
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Every surface wave’s “e2e” is `generate_html` / visible-text-node assertions plus `node --check` on script blocks, with a JSON “control→handler→capability→state” trace. That is unit-level render theater, not a user path. A competitor product proves end-to-end by driving the real UI (click Diagnose, attach from the session list, open a .docx, stop a live session) against a real or high-fidelity Anchor process and asserting the live DOM/state. This plan can pass every scoped pytest while the real control remains unbound in the served app, the click never reaches the handler, or the preview path only works in the fixture harness. “Works end-to-end” in the North Star is a user claim; HTML-string GREEN is a competitor’s favorite false green. Require at least one real interaction path per North-Star surface (or an honest named degradation if the host cannot automate UI), not only rendered-string conformance.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control … Doctor diagnose and session attach … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: W3 freezes PRESENT/STUB/ABSENT from “captured-once, replayed-many” transcripts so John is not needed live. A competitor inventory re-probes the live v1.2 surface (or fails closed to unknown) at freeze and again before each surface wave GO. One-shot replay lets a control go PRESENT on an old transcript while the real handler is now a no-op, canned, or unbound — then W13–W16 “wire it / build it” decisions and dead-control audits inherit a lie. That is exactly how dead Diagnose/Retry/restart survive a “capability-backed” plan. Capture-once is fine for offline unit tests; it is illegal as the sole authority for PRESENT that authorizes shipping a live control. Either re-probe at freeze + pre-surface GO, or treat aged transcripts as unknown and force re-inventory — never PRESENT-by-replay alone.

findings.section: Wave 11 (E2 as_of provisional usage/time); Wave 2 E2 rules; Success criteria usage/time/cost
findings.criterion: silent zero … unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero … Cost never fabricates dollars (and usage surfaces that claim numbers must not fabricate confidence)
findings.message: Cost correctly bans E2 and fabricated dollars. Usage/time still allow a signed E2 “provisional” count with an as_of stamp. A competitor usage surface never shows a numeral until the rollup is PROVEN; provisional is still a confident wrong answer — the defect class the honesty gate names. An as_of stamp next to a wrong count is a disclaimer, not honesty. If the rollup is UNPROVEN, the only competitive-grade states are pending/unknown/measurement_failed — not a number under E2. Close E2 for any user-visible count that criterion 3 surfaces (usage and time), or the plan institutionalizes silent-wrong (cousin of silent zero) on half of the usage/time/cost criterion while being strict only on dollars.

findings.section: Wave 13 done-when / GWT; criterion 4 Doctor real diagnose
findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose … real diagnose (success criteria: Doctor real diagnose; banner payload)
findings.message: W13’s proof that diagnosis is “real” is: two induced faults produce *different* rendered findings. A competitor Doctor is real when findings track injected root causes with structured, checkable claims (and non-canned content), not when two templates differ. Seeded multi-branch theater still “differs” and still fails the North Star’s “real diagnose.” Require fault→expected finding contracts (or inventory-backed golden transcripts of real diagnose behavior), plus an explicit ban on fixed seed strings — variance alone is a competitor-beatable bar.

findings.section: Success criteria; Wave 13 banner_handoff; North Star “health, usage, or diagnose”
findings.criterion: 4/health to every health-claiming surface, or the plan closes “diagnose” while leaving health claims free to silent-zero and mislabelled-empty.
findings.message: Usage and diagnose get full surface trains; “health” is reduced to banner→Doctor payload handoff. There is no wave that inventories every surface that *claims* health (banner copy, health tile, status chrome) and forces ok/unknown/empty/zero_measured/failed with unknown≠empty. A competitor health strip that shows green/empty/zero without evidence loses users to an honest unknown. Expand

findings.section: Wave 3 STUB→build it; Wave 5 DOC-TRIO-AMENDMENT / WAVE-LIST-FREEZE
findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor + attach without dead controls; surfaces work E2E or named failure
findings.message: The competitive product scopes “build it vs wire it” before committing the surface train. This plan discovers STUBs in W3, then relies on mid-build wave insertion and re-freeze. That is honest process, but it leaves the delivered North Star set unbounded: enough STUBs and the conjunction scorer (2-per-criterion / 4 total) or schedule pressure pushes E1/E3 exits or dropped surfaces. Competitor plans either (a) pre-budget a fixed maximum of build-it waves with explicit cut-line to named unavailable states, or (b) inventory before freeze with a hard cap on unsigned STUBs. Without a hard scope/cut-line tied to the ten criteria, “freeze then amend forever” is how dead controls become signed exits or unshipped work while process stays GREEN.

findings.section: Wave 1 task triple; Wave 21 S1; Steward/S1 North Star clause
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart … Doctor diagnose and session attach; Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: S1-as-sole North Star declaration is correct and must stay. Competitor *engineering* still re-runs the verification task triple (or an automated subset) after each surface wave that claims a verb in that triple — attach after W10, diagnose after W13/W14, stop/restart after W15/W16 — so failures are cheap and early. This plan explicitly avoids live John until S1 and relies on fixture/fault injection in between. That maximizes late BUILD_BLOCKING discovery after twenty waves of process and partial product. Keep S1 as the only *declaration* of North Star met; add mandatory mid-build task-triple checkpoints (or host-automated equivalents) so “not a silent claim” is not paired with “first real user proof is also the last.”

findings.topic: nine infra waves before any surface fix
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart … without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty, or a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: A competitor team ships the smallest honest product first: named-state primitive + the dead controls John hits daily (Diagnose, Retry/attach, restart, binary preview). This plan serializes nine Phase-0/1/2 waves (task triple, exit register, inventory, rollup gate, freeze, named state, cost_state, conformance harness, trace/fault/log) before any Phase-3 surface can start, then serializes surfaces through W19. The machinery serves honesty, but the critical path maximizes calendar risk that S1 fails or exits accumulate. Competitor sequencing: W6-class named state + one or two highest-pain surfaces in parallel with inventory/rollup, freeze only what those surfaces need. As written, the plan optimizes for process completeness over competitive time-to-honest-UX on the North Star’s daily path.

findings.section: Wave 17 File preview; Wave 3 inventory “preview path”
findings.criterion: a preview that dumps raw binary … File preview human-friendly Office/PDF via shared path
findings.message: W17 “reuses the already-working new-window renderer.” That is a competitor foot-gun: if the shared path is STUB, format-incomplete, or only works for one type, the wave becomes a thin router over a broken dependency and binary can still appear on alternate code paths. Inventory must prove PRESENT per format (docx/pptx/xlsx/pdf) with transcripts of human-friendly output *before* W17 is allowed to claim reuse; if STUB, W17 is a build-it wave for the renderer itself, not a wire-up. Competitor products do not ship “delegate to shared path” without per-format evidence the path actually humanizes those bytes.

findings.section: Wave 21 release_guard.py; North Star v1.1.x clause; Wave 1 containment
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: Containment smoke protects planning-path writes and root foreign Foreman artifacts; the only explicit “not publishable to v1.1.x” guard is W21. A competitor release process fails closed on branch/channel from the first product commit (W6+). Late-only release_guard allows accidental packaging, tag, or channel bleed during surface waves. Move branch/channel non-publish checks to an early always-on gate (or extend W1 containment to publish surfaces), not only the terminal wave.

findings.topic: restart dual-control audit is HTML count only
findings.criterion: exactly one restart control per restart context — work or not shown; no dual competing controls
findings.message: The audit asserts control count == 1 in rendered HTML. A competitor also proves behavioral exclusivity: only one control can trigger restart for that context (no hidden keyboard path, menu duplicate, or second entry point that restarts with a different preserved/lost contract). Count-of-buttons GREEN with two behavioral restart paths still violates “exactly one restart control per context.” Extend the contract to “exactly one restart *action* per context,” not only one labelled button in the HTML snapshot.

findings.topic: failure-state vocabulary mismatched to UI surfaces
findings.section: Hardening-gate obligations Failure-state table vocabulary; Waves 10–19 failure-states/*
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; named, user-visible state
findings.message: The emitted 0080 vocabulary (dependency-missing, index read/write, rebuild, reconcile, verify, CLI verbs) reads like a storage/index product, not Anchor session/Doctor/cost UI. Wave-local tables partially re-map, but the plan still requires those five rows “per surface (index read/write…).” A competitor names the states the *user* hits (attach timeout, unmeasured cost, inventory unreadable, unsupported preview). If agents fill index-reconcile rows for a Doctor tile, honesty theater returns. Require surface-native failure rows that map 1:1 to NamedState/user-visible strings for each North-Star surface; keep storage vocabulary only where the surface actually is a store/CLI.

reviews.note: Analyst Shark · bored-investor angle. Plan is process-heavy and serial; findings only elevated when they threaten a North Star criterion (delivery of open/run/stop/restart + diagnose/attach honesty, named states, cost truth, no v1.1.x ship, S1-only NS claim).

findings.section: Success criteria; Waves 10–19; Wave 1 task triple
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.message: The North Star leads with four verbs. The plan names a verification task triple of open/run/stop-restart in W1, then spends surface waves on attach, usage, cost, Doctor, stop summary, restart, preview, projects, and cadence. There is no wave whose done-when is “open real Anchor work works end-to-end or fails with a named state,” and none for “run.” Stop and restart get W15–W16; attach gets W10. Open and run are either assumed already perfect (unproven in this draft) or silently omitted. A bored investor funds open/run/stop/restart; this plan only budgets the last half and a side attach. Either add open/run surface waves bound to inventory PRESENT|STUB|ABSENT, or freeze an explicit inventory verdict that open/run are PRESENT with transcripts and no further work—do not leave the first two North Star verbs as ambient hope.

findings.criterion: without meeting … a silent zero, a mislabelled empty … (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: W11’s acceptance says a PROVEN rollup that “genuinely returns zero rows for today” renders empty, “distinct from both unknown and zero_measured.” Zero rows for a measured day is measured zero activity, not an empty collection in the “no data domain” sense. Teaching the surface to label measured absence of events as empty reintroduces the exact mislabelled-empty / silent-zero class the North Star bans—especially once cost and usage sit on the same chrome. Empty must mean “no series / no scope,” zero_measured must mean “rollup ran and the total is 0,” unknown must mean “we did not successfully read.” Fix the Given/When/Then and the failure-state table before this wave can claim criterion 3.

findings.section: Wave 5 — Wave-list freeze + doc-trio amendment; Wave 3 inventory
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: W3 can reclassify any control to STUB → “build it,” and W5’s DOC-TRIO-AMENDMENT lets those waves be inserted indefinitely with only a re-freeze. There is no cap on inserted waves, no “must still hit S1 on this effort,” and no rule that STUB on a North Star control is either built in-plan or closed with a signed exit—not deferred forever by amendment churn. Bored-investor read: inventory is a blank check that can keep surface delivery (Diagnose, attach, restart) off the calendar forever while still looking “governed.” Bound it: max inserted waves, or mandatory E1/build-now decision per North Star control at freeze, with conjunction scorer already treating serial deferral as re-baseline risk.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: The plan’s own law says a property named without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER—and conversely that obligations must be enforced. Honesty (failure-state table; unknown≠empty) is partially wave-local. Idempotence (repeat-invocation), boundedness (numeric bound + refusal), containment (escape-attempt), and storage vocabulary (atomic temp+fsync+rename, cross-process lock, concurrency test) appear as global checklists with no wave that names the bound, the refusal path, the escape test, or the durable write path for preference store (W18), cost migration (W7), inventory/rollup artifacts, or EXECUTION-LOG. Claiming durability/honesty guarantees while product surfaces only assert “three labels differ” is confident process theater: the North Star needs failure honesty on real health/usage/diagnose paths, not a second copy of journal 0080 with unchecked boxes. Either map each obligation to a concrete wave acceptance criterion or drop the claim so the plan does not advertise unenforced guarantees.

findings.section: Wave 6 NamedState; Hardening failure-state table vocabulary; wave-local failure-states/*
findings.criterion: fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: W6 ships NamedState (ok, unknown, empty, zero_measured, pending, unmeasured, measurement_failed, timeout, cannot_retry). Hardening vocabulary demands five different rows (dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid) with status codes per surface verb. Surface waves only promise “unknown and empty as separate rows.” No mapping table says which NamedState is dependency-returns-garbage vs backing-store-unreadable. Two parallel honesty languages means implementers will satisfy the easier checklist and leave the required five as prose. That is how “named state” becomes “we showed unknown somewhere.” Require one vocabulary (or an explicit bijection enforced by the table validator) before any surface wave is GO.

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: Nine waves of ledgers, exit registers, inventory, rollup gates, freeze stamps, named-state primitives, cost enums, conformance harnesses, and trace plumbing precede the first user-facing attach honesty (W10). None of W1–W9 lets John open, run, stop, restart, diagnose, or attach on v1.2. Bored investor: all capital can be spent and still deliver zero North Star verbs if Phase 0/1/2 stalls. Process floor is defensible; a fully serial nine-wave tax before any vertical slice is not. Collapse or parallelize Phase 2 primitives with one thin end-to-end path (e.g. attach or Diagnose) so a mid-build halt still leaves a working surface, not only green pytest on governance modules.

findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose and session attach … Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose
findings.message: Attach (W10) blocks usage (W11) blocks cost (W12) blocks Doctor (W13–14) blocks stop (W15) blocks restart (W16) blocks preview (W17) blocks projects (W18) blocks cadence (W19). Doctor does not need usage tiles; restart does not need PDF preview; cadence does not need projects collapse. Artificial total order delays diagnose and restart—the named North Star inclusions—behind unrelated surfaces. Investor view: longest possible critical path maximizes calendar risk of never reaching S1 with the verbs that matter. Re-express dependencies as true data/contract edges (named_state, rollup_registry, inventory row) only; allow parallel surface waves after freeze.

findings.section: Wave 1 task triple; Wave 5 freeze; Wave 21 S1
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build. / John can open, run, stop, and restart…
findings.message: W1 forbids E5 on the task triple and HALTs without John’s dated line; W5 requires John’s Phase-1 verdict review before any surface wave; W21 requires live S1. S1 as the only North Star claim is correct and in-scope. Stacking two additional hard live-John gates before any product wave means the build cannot advance through process phases without calendar attendance—while the North Star still depends on a fourth live session at the end. Bored investor: three human appointments on the critical path, two of them before value. Keep S1 sacred; make W1/W5 either pre-seedable from a prior signed artifact with expiry, or allow orchestration to proceed on captured transcripts with a single re-confirm at freeze—not a hard stop that strandsthe entire NS delivery on scheduling.

findings.criterion: without meeting … a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: W17 intent and deliverables assume “the already-working new-window path” and only “route” formats through it. That assumption is not bound to a W3 PRESENT verdict or a freeze delta. If inventory says STUB/ABSENT, this wave as written ships theater or a dead path—exactly the raw-binary / dead-control failure mode. Freeze must either insert a build-it wave for the shared renderer or mark ABSENT with a named unsupported state for all Office/PDF; W17 must not hard-code “already-working.”

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: There is no milestone where a single North Star verb is done under real UI with named failure states before the full ten-criteria matrix. Governance is front-loaded; product is back-loaded. If conjunction re-baseline HALTs at four exits mid-surface phase, John may have exit_register.py and freeze stamps but still meet dead Diagnose or dishonest attach. Define an ordered minimum slice (e.g. attach + stop + one restart context + Diagnose) that may reach a partial honest state without claiming full North Star—explicitly partial, not silent green—so investment is not all-or-nothing at W21.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: W7 adds a schema migration and backfill to unmeasured, and bans $0.00 fabrication at render time. It does not specify failed-migration behavior, partial backfill, or what the UI shows if cost_state column is missing mid-deploy—i.e. dependency-missing / backing-store paths from the plan’s own failure vocabulary. A half-migrated DB is the classic path back to “0 ⇒ subscription” or blank dollars. Require named measurement_failed/unmeasured when schema or backfill is incomplete, and a gate that refuses measured rendering until migration attestation is host-verified.

findings.message: Branch/channel non-publication is only enforced in the final wave. Intermediate commits on a mistaken branch or packaging path are unchecked until S1. Cheap refinement: run release_guard (or a one-line branch assertion) from W1 containment smoke onward so the collaborator boundary is continuous, not a last-day checkbox.
